audio.label: positive
audio.text: At the river, he stopped. The bridge was gone. Rain had turned the water brown and violent. He stepped back, ran, and threw himself into the flood. The current pulled him under. He fought toward the light, caught a branch, and dragged himself onto the far bank. Farther along, three men blocked the road. A knife flashed. Melos struck the man holding it with his walking stick and ran uphill, their shouts following him. By afternoon, every step hurt. Blood stained his feet. He fell beside a rock and tried to rise, but his legs would not obey. He could wait here. Someone might find him. He could go home. His friend would die. For one terrible moment, that seemed easier than getting up.

audio.label: positive
audio.text: Beyond the river, attackers blocked the road. One grabbed his arm. Another swung a stick. Melos struck out, broke free, and stumbled past them. Their angry shouts followed him, but he did not look back. By afternoon, pain filled every step. Then his legs gave way. He lay with his face against the earth. The city was still far away. He could not reach it. He could not even stand. He could stay here. No one would find him before sunset. His friend would die, but he would live. For one terrible moment, the thought brought relief. Then he remembered those warm fingers around his hand.
